question_en:
The community pottery studio needs to make test tiles for all the glazes in the list shown in the image. Please answer:

What conclusion does the official product data give for each glaze when used on tableware surfaces? Provide a complete itemized table including 'Color Code, Product Name, and Group'. Which glazes are included in the 'Standard Vessel Test' and 'Decorative-Only Test' groups, and what is the count for each?

The answer must include a table with 'Image Position—Color Code—Product Name—Official Conclusion for Tableware Surface Use—Group', followed by the list of glazes and their respective counts for both groups after the table.

# Detailed Simulated Retrieval Trajectory · 1-1-E01

## Step 01 · inspect_image / Determine Input and Full Scope

Action: Open the current unique input image in the images for this problem, and register items one by one according to the order in the image.

Evidence Observation (Archived Evidence Summary): The input consists of 12 glaze sample tiles arranged in 3 rows and 4 columns, with color code text removed; first find official samples by position, crackle/flow texture, and color blocks; color codes and product names must be obtained through image comparison.

Result of this step: Fix the 12 members; complete full registration first, then filter or calculate.

## Step 02 · parse_task / Establish Fields to Query and Output Constraints

Action: Read question_zh-new, separating information confirmable from the image from information requiring external lookup.

Evidence Observation (Archived Evidence Summary): Check manufacturer instructions for tableware surface use for each product style; having only color appearance or a Food Safe mark is insufficient to substitute for a Dinnerware Safe conclusion. This time, output only the two groups: Standard Vessel Test and Decorative-Only Test.

Result of this step: Subsequent web searches are only to fill in these fields; finally, output strictly according to the requirements at the end of the question.

## Step 03 · image_search + open_catalog / Locate the Same Official Sample Set

Action: Example query: ceramic glaze sample diagonal textured tile blue green Mayco stoneware; compare the sample's diagonal embossed texture, crackle structure, and color block layout, then verify the product card on the official category page.

Evidence Observation (Archived Evidence Summary): The first 11 items correspond to product samples in the Stoneware list; the 12th item, a white raised crackle piece, requires further checking in Stoneware Specialty. Generally, the Stoneware freeze page does not have an independent card for SW-403, so one cannot claim to have read its card on that page.

Evidence Links:
- Stoneware Catalog: https://www.maycocolors.com/color/fired/stoneware/
- Specialty Catalog: https://www.maycocolors.com/color/fired/stoneware-specialty/
- Official Product/Color Code/Image URL Cross-Reference Table: https://www.maycocolors.com/color-swatches-csv-download/

Result of this step: On 2026-10-11, perform a supplementary check on the official color card CSV page to complete the SW-403 product page and original image URL; extract links for other products from already saved category pages.

## Step 04 · open_manual / Read Tableware Suitability Rules and Exceptions

Action: In the fixed product manual, check the Stoneware Classic safety instructions and the Mudcrack special chapter, distinguishing between printed page numbers and PDF page order.

Evidence Observation (Archived Evidence Summary): Classic printed pages 60–61 correspond to PDF pages 63–64; Mudcrack printed pages 66–67 correspond to PDF pages 69–70. Ordinary Classic is suitable under the conditions of firing per manufacturer instructions and having a non-textured surface; SW-132 has a clear exception; Mudcrack is recommended for decorative use only due to its surface characteristics. There are other exceptions in the current full series; do not generalize rules from the old manual to all products outside this problem.
